title: aid-auto-resume/1
description: The single authoritative continuation pointer for a run that handed work to a background job supervisor. Written EAGERLY — before aid-job.sh spawns anything — and deleted only when the last outstanding background job of the run has been collected. It exists because a controller that dies mid-EXECUTE cannot write anything on its way out: the truth about 'is a resume required?' has to be derivable from what the controller provably left behind, never from a state a dying process was supposed to store. Consumers therefore DERIVE `awaiting_host_resume` as 'this artifact exists AND there is no liveness signal within the stall threshold'; the state is never stored anywhere.

plan_id.description: Plan this run belongs to (e.g. P076), or the literal 'unknown' when the epic id carries no plan number.

job_id.description: The supervised job this pointer refers to, OR the literal 'pending' — the value the PRE-SPAWN write carries. 'pending' is not a gap in the record: it says 'a job was about to be started in jobs_dir with command_fingerprint', which is exactly what the recovery scan needs to decide whether one actually was.

jobs_dir.description: Directory holding the run's supervised job records — the directory the pending-recovery scan walks.

gate.description: Gate whose command was delegated to the supervisor.

command_fingerprint.description: aid-job.sh's own sha256-over-NUL-joined-argv fingerprint. This is what a pending-recovery scan MATCHES ON when job_id is still 'pending' (or when the crash landed between spawn and rewrite): it identifies the job the dead controller meant to start, without trusting a job id that was never written.

expected_terminal_states.description: aid-job.sh's terminal vocabulary, verbatim. A resume that finds the job in one of these states collects it; anything else means the job is still in flight or was lost.

safe_next_action.description: The exact command to run, FULLY RESOLVED at write time — real plugin path, literal epic and run ids. The pattern forbids '<' so no '<epic_id>'-style placeholder can ever persist here: a continuation instruction a human has to fill in is not a continuation instruction.
